# Lab 27.4: Event-Driven BigQuery with Eventarc

## What We Are Going to Do
Trigger a Cloud Run service automatically whenever a BigQuery job finishes or a table is created, using Eventarc and audit logs.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Deploy a small receiver service.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">mkdir -p bq_events &amp;&amp; cd bq_events
cat &gt; main.py &lt;&lt;'EOF'
import os, json
from flask import Flask, request
app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route("/", methods=["POST"])
def receive():
    event = request.get_json(silent=True) or {}
    payload = event.get("protoPayload", {})
    print(json.dumps({"method": payload.get("methodName"), "resource": payload.get("resourceName"),
                      "who": payload.get("authenticationInfo", {}).get("principalEmail")}))
    return ("ok", 200)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", 8080)))
EOF
echo "flask" &gt; requirements.txt
gcloud run deploy bq-events --source=. --region=us-central1 --no-allow-unauthenticated --quiet
cd ..</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[CLI] Create the Eventarc trigger.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud services enable eventarc.googleapis.com
PROJECT_NUMBER=$(gcloud projects describe $PROJECT_ID --format="value(projectNumber)")
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT_ID \
  --member=serviceAccount:$PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/eventarc.eventReceiver --quiet
gcloud eventarc triggers create bq-table-created --location=us \
  --destination-run-service=bq-events --destination-run-region=us-central1 \
  --event-filters="type=google.cloud.audit.log.v1.written" \
  --event-filters="serviceName=bigquery.googleapis.com" \
  --event-filters="methodName=google.cloud.bigquery.v2.TableService.InsertTable" \
  --service-account=$PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[CLI] Fire the event.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq mk --table lab20.event_test id:INT64</span>
</code></pre>

4. **[Console] See it arrive.** Open **Cloud Run → bq-events → Logs**. A log line shows the method, the new table and who created it.

5. **Ideas.** The same pattern can start a pipeline when a load job completes, notify a team when a dataset is deleted, or apply policy tags when a new table appears.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Event source | BigQuery audit logs |
| Filter | Service and method name |
| Target | Cloud Run service |
| Use | React to BigQuery changes automatically |
